target_customer: Developers and (from 2026) enterprises wanting searchable, AI-usable records of employees' computer work
problem: Work context on screens is lost; screenpipe records screen and audio locally and exposes it to LLM agents.
business_model: Source-available/open-source app with a paid desktop licence (vendor-stated lifetime licence) and enterprise offering

founders.name: Louis Beaumont
previous_startups: Video-game bots business started at age 14 (per YC page)

competitors.name: Rewind AI
competitors.what: Mac-only personal screen memory app (per screenpipe's own comparison, vendor claim)

competitors.name: Microsoft Recall
competitors.what: Windows 11 feature requiring Copilot+ PCs; closed source

technical_complexity.rationale: Continuous cross-platform screen/audio capture, OCR and local indexing exposed to LLMs; engineering heavy but standard components.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source origin and rapidly commoditising capture layer; large platform vendors offer similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft shipped Recall for Copilot+ PCs; screenpipe's own blog says Rewind pivoted to Limitless and Meta killed it (vendor claim, unverified).

market_need_then: Rewind AI and Microsoft Recall launching showed demand for screen memory; screenpipe cites 20K+ GitHub stars (YC page, self-reported).

branding.domain_note: Used the screenpi.pe domain hack; screenpipe.com now serves the site (blog URLs redirect from screenpi.pe to screenpipe.com); acquisition date unknown
branding.community_and_virality: 20K+ GitHub stars and about 70 contributors cited by the company; mostly self-reported

brand_strength.rationale: Open-source community presence, but sources are largely the company's own.

outcome_analysis: Too early to judge: screenpipe, an open-source screen-memory tool started in 2024, joined YC in Summer 2026 and reports 20K+ GitHub stars. Its license reportedly moved to source-available and Rewind and Microsoft Recall define the competition; no verified funding or revenue exists.
notes: Directory says founded 2026, search results say 2024 (Sep 2024 r/software launch post); 2024 used. Unverified funding: company blog Feb 2025 said it was raising $5M (a target); an aggregator lists $2.8M seed. Neither recorded. Competitor sources are the vendor's own comparison pages and one Reddit post. Licence status conflicts (MIT vs source-available commercial licence). Brand details limited. Directory status Active.
